topic: attempted low-band suppression coefficients: invalid, predictor saturates
idea: in this architecture u = (s + g*mic)/(1 + g*Hhat), so a large |Hhat| inside 250-470 Hz should attenuate the loop band there while leaving the speech band untouched
comparison: with zero coefficients the same gain of -8 dB was clean (mode share 0.12) and the listener confirmed clear amplification, so the new coefficients made it strictly worse at every tested gain
root_cause: the prediction sum q*ref exceeds the signed-24-bit range long before the intended loop attenuation is reached: reaching |g*Hhat| ~ 1 at 360 Hz needs |Hhat| ~ 2.5, which the fixed-point predictor cannot carry
conclusion: low-band suppression through the existing prediction path is not feasible at the required magnitude in this word width; it would need either a different filter placement (a forward-path filter before the gain, not the predictor) or a wider internal format
not_claimed: does not show that low-band suppression is impossible in principle
only that this placement and width cannot deliver it
recommended_owner: B decides the filter placement; C keeps the measurement protocol; A loads and re-runs the board comparison once a valid design exists
